Create a Philips Hue Application Key

Source: R/client.R
hue_create_app_key.Rd

Sends POST https://<ip>/api to register a new application key (hue-application-key) and optional Entertainment DTLS clientkey on a local Philips Hue Bridge (v2 or Bridge Pro).

Usage

hue_create_app_key(
  ip,
  app_name = "huer",
  instance_name = Sys.info()[["nodename"]],
  generate_client_key = TRUE,
  verify_ssl = FALSE,
  ca_cert = NULL,
  timeout = 10
)

Arguments

ip

Character scalar. IPv4/IPv6 address or hostname of the Hue Bridge.

app_name

Character scalar. Application identifier (1-20 ASCII characters). Defaults to "huer".

instance_name

Character scalar. Device or host identifier (1-19 ASCII characters). Defaults to the local machine hostname.

generate_client_key

Logical scalar. If TRUE (default), also requests a 32-character hex clientkey for Hue Entertainment DTLS streaming.

verify_ssl

Logical scalar. Whether to verify the bridge TLS certificate. Defaults to FALSE for initial local LAN onboarding; supply ca_cert and verify_ssl = TRUE when verifying against the Hue Root CA.

ca_cert

Optional path to a PEM CA certificate bundle.

timeout

Numeric scalar. Request timeout in seconds. Defaults to 10.

Value

A tbl_json tibble containing username (the hue-application-key) and, when requested, clientkey.

Details

Before calling hue_create_app_key(), you must physically press the round link button on top of the Philips Hue Bridge. If the link button was not pressed within the last 30 seconds, the bridge returns error type 101 (link button not pressed).

See also

hue_auth(), hue_bridge(), hue_get_application_id()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Press the physical link button on your Hue Bridge first, then run:
creds <- hue_create_app_key("192.168.1.50", app_name = "huer")
hue_auth(ip = "192.168.1.50", app_key = creds$username[[1]])
} # }
